questions.q: What did Edward Jenner use to create the first vaccine?
a: Cowpox pus, after noticing milkmaids seemed immune to smallpox
Weakened smallpox virus grown in a laboratory
Blood serum taken from recovered patients
A mixture of herbs used by local farmers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Jenner injected cowpox material in 1796 after observing the milkmaids' immunity.

questions.q: What is the adaptive immune response?
a: Cells that meet a threat duplicate into cells that remember it
Receptors that block every foreign substance at once
The swelling that follows an injury
The body's first reaction to a paper cut
questions.why: Lesson 1 says T and B cells multiply after contact so they can recognize the same threat later.

a: Act as molecular messengers that coordinate the immune response
Carry oxygen to cells throughout the body
Break down food in the digestive tract
Form the physical barrier of the skin
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes cytokines as proteins that tell cells when to start or stop an immune response.

questions.q: What happens when cytokines are overproduced?
a: Autoimmune disease can develop, such as rheumatoid arthritis
The immune system shuts down completely
Allergies disappear over time
Wounds heal more slowly
questions.why: Lesson 2 links an excess of cytokines such as TNF to autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.q: What does immune checkpoint therapy involve?
a: Blocking a receptor so T cells keep attacking cancer instead of switching off
Injecting cytokines directly into a tumour
Removing the tumour surgically before treatment
Strengthening the innate immune system with vaccines
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that blocking the receptor lets immune cells continue destroying the tumour.
